title: Four Companies' Capex: $539B. NVIDIA Data Center Revenue: $278B. The Filings Don't Connect Them.

7.narration: That quarter's filing put hyperscalers near half of data center sales. NVIDIA later moved a customer into that category, recasting it to about 57 percent.

8.narration: Matched to the June quarter, the same comparison read 52 percent. The revenue and the capex sit in separate filings; none links them.

10.narration: NVIDIA's books show about 216 billion of revenue in its fiscal 2026, about nine-tenths of it from its Data Center platform.

15.narration: Cash paid for property and equipment was lower, at 19.4 billion. Of total capex, Hood said, roughly half went to short-lived GPUs and CPUs.

51.narration: In February, Amazon forecast about 200 billion. A third-party transcript of its July call has Andy Jassy near 220 billion, citing memory costs.

52.narration: Microsoft's figure went down instead. In April, Amy Hood put calendar-year capex near 190 billion, about 25 billion from component pricing.

54.narration: That call also moved building depreciation to 25 years from 15, effective fiscal 2027. Hood expected capex to rise year over year.

55.narration: Alphabet CFO Anat Ashkenazi raised its range to 195 to 205 billion. She said spending would increase significantly the year after.

56.narration: On the earnings call, that higher range came with Google Cloud growing 82 percent and a backlog of about 514 billion.

57.narration: These forecasts use different spending definitions. None says how much of it, if any, would become NVIDIA revenue.
